App Development

PWA or Native App: A Business Decision Guide

Compare a browser-based app with an installed mobile app using device needs, distribution, offline behaviour and maintenance.

By DevMania · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read
Share on LinkedInShare on WhatsApp

In this guide

Start with the required experienceTest the hardest requirement earlyConsider how users arriveBudget for the whole lifecycleWrite a decision note

Start with the required experience

A progressive web app uses web technologies and can offer an app-like experience, with capabilities depending on browser and platform support. A native app is built for a device platform. Neither label automatically makes a product better. Start by listing what users need to do and the devices on which they will do it.

Test the hardest requirement early

A field-service product may need camera access, reliable offline entry and background activity. A customer portal may mostly display records and accept forms. Build a small proof of concept around the most demanding requirement before committing to a platform. Browser capability should be verified on the actual target devices.

Consider how users arrive

A public service discovered through a link has different distribution needs from an internal app installed on company devices. Ask whether people will use it once or every day. For occasional tasks, opening a link may be preferable to an installation step. Frequent users may value a dedicated installed experience.

Budget for the whole lifecycle

Count design, testing, releases and support across the platforms you promise to support. Shared code can reduce duplication, but it does not eliminate platform-specific testing. Include responsibility for updates when devices or browsers change. Store distribution also introduces submission and release processes that need an owner.

Write a decision note

Document the required capabilities, target devices, distribution plan and known compromises. Include the proof-of-concept findings rather than relying on a generic comparison chart. Revisit the decision when the product requirements change. A responsive web first release can be a sensible step, but only if it meets the users’ actual workflow.
